Selling · A guide to your next move

A little preparation. A stronger first impression.

Where to focus before your home is photographed.

01

Begin with the welcome

A tidy entrance, clear pathways and a clean front door create a straightforward introduction. Let the home itself lead the first impression.

02

Edit, rather than erase

Clear surfaces and reduce visual clutter while keeping rooms understandable. Buyers should be able to see the space without every room losing its sense of purpose.

03

Let the light do its work

Clean windows and open suitable curtains or blinds for photography. Replace failed bulbs and consider consistent lighting from room to room.

04

Make a short repair list

Identify visible maintenance items and discuss priorities before committing to work. Keep records of completed repairs and relevant property information.

05

Prepare for an honest presentation

Photographs and copy should represent the property accurately. Avoid hiding important limitations or making promises about features that have not been verified.

General editorial guidance prepared for this design concept. This is not legal, financial or property-specific advice.
